pictures.scene: Lucas van Valckenborch, The Tower of Babel — the tower going up ring upon ring out of the plain until the top of it is lost in the pale sky, every storey full of arches and cranes and little sheds, carts and workmen crawling over the ramps around the bottom of it, the sea lying off to one side, and down in front on the rock a man in red pointing the whole thing out to another, why do the nations rage and the peoples plot in vain
pictures.name: pd_valckenborch_the_tower_of_babel

pictures.scene: Jacques-Louis David, The Oath of the Horatii — the bare stone hall with its round arches, the three brothers braced forward in their red cloaks and sandals with their arms shot out straight together, and the grey-bearded father standing against them holding the three swords up in one fist so that the blades fan out between them, every man in the picture swearing the same thing, the kings of the earth take their stand and the rulers gather together
pictures.name: pd_david_the_oath_of_the_horatii

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, The Conspiracy of Claudius Civilis — the long table glowing out of a brown dark, the one-eyed chieftain sitting at the head of it in a tall gold crown and a gold robe with his sword held straight up, the lords ranged along the table leaning in to lay their own blades across his so the swords cross in a sheaf over the light, one of them pushing a dish forward and another come up out of a chair with his back to us, the whole room swearing itself into a conspiracy, against the LORD and against His Anointed One, let us break Their chains and cast away Their cords
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_the_conspiracy_of_claudius_civilis

pictures.scene: Jan van Eyck, God Enthroned — the enthroned figure close up and straight on, a triple jewelled tiara of pearls and sapphires set on His head, long dark hair down over both shoulders and a deep red mantle clasped across His breast with a great round brooch of pearls and blue stones, the orphrey bands sewn with crosses falling either side of Him, one hand lifting at the edge of the picture, and behind His head the gold rays going out all round into a gold arch lettered in Latin, the One enthroned in heaven laughs, the Lord taunts them
pictures.name: pd_van_eyck_god_enthroned_ghent_altarpiece

pictures.scene: Joseph Wright of Derby, Vesuvius in Eruption — the molten rock running red in rivers down the black slope along the whole bottom of the picture, the bay beyond it lying quiet with the moon laying a long silver track across the water, and the smoke of the mountain spread right over the sky in a dark reddish pall with the moon half swallowed in a gap of torn cloud, then He rebukes them in His anger and terrifies them in His fury
pictures.name: pd_wright_of_derby_vesuvius_in_eruption

pictures.scene: Gustav Bauernfeind, View of Jerusalem — the whole city seen across the valley in the early light, the great retaining wall of the temple platform running right along under it and the blue dome standing up at the end of the courts, flat roofs and towers and cypresses packed away behind, the bare hillside with its olive trees falling to the path in front, and a knot of pilgrims in dark coats and a woman with a basket on her head climbing the stony track toward the gates, I have installed My King on Zion, upon My holy mountain
pictures.name: pd_bauernfeind_zion

pictures.scene: Joachim Patinir, The Baptism of Christ — Christ standing in the river with a white cloth knotted at His waist and His hands laid together in prayer, looking straight out of the picture, John leaning in from the bank in a rough brown mantle with his hand held flat over Christ's head, the white dove coming down out of a gap in the cloud and the Father seen up in the broken light above it, the blue country and the rocks and the far hills opening out behind, I will proclaim the decree spoken to Me by the LORD, You are My Son today I have become Your Father
pictures.name: pd_patinir_baptism

pictures.scene: Claude Lorrain, A Seaport at Sunrise — the sun just up out of a flat calm sea and laying a pale track straight toward us, a round stone fort standing out on the point at one side and masts of ships showing far out at the other, a lateen-rigged vessel moored in close with her yard down, boatmen in short tunics poling a loaded skiff in to the shore and handing the bales down, and the timbers lying across the beach in front, ask Me and I will make the nations Your inheritance, the ends of the earth Your possession
pictures.name: pd_claude_lorrain_a_seaport_at_sunrise

pictures.scene: Giovanni Paolo Panini, Roman Ruins — the broken ground covered with the wreck of a city, carved cornices and drums of columns and a great stone block tipped over in the foreground, a bronze emperor still up on his rearing horse on a pedestal at the edge of the rubble with the ruined wall behind him, and the country people sitting and standing about among the stones in their rough cloaks as if none of it were theirs, You will break them with an iron scepter, You will shatter them like pottery
pictures.name: pd_panini_ruines

pictures.scene: Diego Velazquez, The Adoration of the Magi — the mother sitting in a rose bodice and a white head cloth with a faint ring of gold behind her head, the child upright on her knee wrapped close in white linen and looking straight out of the picture, and the great men come in out of the dark and bending down to Him, the first kneeling in a yellow cloak and holding up a gold cup in both gloved hands, another behind in a red mantle and a white ruff with a covered vessel, the rest crowded in at the edges watching, therefore be wise O kings, be admonished O judges of the earth
pictures.name: pd_velazquez_adoration_of_the_magi

pictures.scene: Jean-Francois Millet, The Angelus — the peasant woman standing alone in the dug field at evening in a bonnet and a long work apron, her head bowed right down and her hands folded up at her breast, the basket of potatoes at her feet and the barrow left behind her, the flat land running away under a heavy gold sky with the church spire small on the far horizon where the bell is ringing, serve the LORD with fear and rejoice with trembling
pictures.name: pd_millet_the_angelus

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, The Return of the Prodigal Son — the son down on his knees with his face buried against his father in a torn pale coat, his head shaved and one worn shoe fallen off his bare foot, and the old father bent over him in a great red cloak laying both hands flat on his shoulders and saying nothing, the elder brother standing off at the side in a dark red cloak with his hands shut together, watching, and two more looking on out of the brown dark behind, kiss the Son lest He be angry and you perish in your rebellion
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_the_return_of_the_prodigal_son

pictures.scene: Johannes Oertel, Rock of Ages — the stone cross standing up solid out of the sea with the water breaking white all round its foot, a woman in a white robe and a red mantle washed up against the rock and holding on to the arm of the cross with both hands, her face turned up out of the spray, and down in the foam below her a drowning hand still reaching for a broken spar going past, when His wrath ignites in an instant, blessed are all who take refuge in Him
pictures.name: pd_oertel_rock_of_ages

lines.text: Why do the nations rage
and the peoples plot in vain?
The kings of the earth take their stand
and the rulers gather together,
against the LORD and against His Anointed One:
Let us break Their chains and cast away Their cords.
The One enthroned in heaven laughs;
the Lord taunts them.
Then He rebukes them in His anger,
and terrifies them in His fury:
I have installed My King on Zion,
upon My holy mountain.
I will proclaim the decree spoken to Me by the LORD:
You are My Son; today I have become Your Father.
Ask Me, and I will make the nations Your inheritance,
the ends of the earth Your possession.
You will break them with an iron scepter;
You will shatter them like pottery.
Therefore be wise, O kings;
be admonished, O judges of the earth.
Serve the LORD with fear,
and rejoice with trembling.
Kiss the Son, lest He be angry
and you perish in your rebellion,
when His wrath ignites in an instant.
Blessed are all who take refuge in Him.
